headline: Record shipments and wider metal spreads lift earnings
summary_short: Steel Dynamics earned $756M, or $5.26 per diluted share, in Q3 2026 versus $3.69 in Q2 and $2.74 a year ago, on record steel shipments of 3.8 million tons.
summary_long: Consolidated operating income rose $306M, or 44%, sequentially. Steel operating income of $1.0B was 43% higher as the average external selling price rose $102 to $1,400 per ton and scrap cost fell $8 to $404. Fabrication earned $91M with order backlog 50% above a year ago. Aluminum operating losses narrowed 21% to $26M and the unit was EBITDA breakeven. The company repurchased $276M of stock and ended with $2.4B of liquidity.
confidence_notes: Adjusted EBITDA of $1.2B is a non-GAAP figure as presented by the company. Net income q/q change computed from $756M versus $534M. The release gives no numeric forward guidance.

drivers.explanation: Management says steel prices continued to improve and the teams executed well, in a strong domestic market with low customer inventories and historically low imports.
Steel operating income rose on record shipments and metal spread expansion as realized selling prices increased and scrap costs declined.
Energy, non-residential construction, automotive and industrial sectors led steel demand in the quarter.
Aluminum startup losses narrowed 21% sequentially to $26M, though volumes were below expectations due to yield losses at higher speeds.
